source_reviews.independent_solution:
Electrification is a process of broadly using electrical energy in production,
transportation, and everyday life. It is not merely constructing power stations
or using electricity in just one of these domains.

The explanation must connect three problems: obtaining, transmitting, and
applying electrical energy. Generation facilities supply electrical energy.
Transmission facilities deliver that electrical energy to the places of use.
At those places, equipment converts electrical energy into other needed forms.
Generation, delivery, and end use are different roles in one connected system;
delivery is not itself the creation of electrical energy, and generation is not
already the account of how that energy is used.

The selected definitions support explaining generation through fuel thermal,
hydroelectric, and atomic-energy stations using the chains below. They do not
state that every historical example used every station type.

The full written prompt also explicitly requests a connection to the Soviet
historical example. That component remains part of the source task. The seed
provides the historical framing, but no named station, historical programme,
event, quantity, or example of a particular Soviet end-use installation.
Consequently, a seed-only solution can explain the conceptual system in that
historical frame but cannot substantiate a concrete named historical example.
No such example is invented or retrieved here. That unanswerable specific
recall/exemplification component must be recorded if later questions defer it;
conceptual coverage must not be reported as literal full written reproduction.

knows, with lesson historical examples permitted, and classify the examples as
fuel thermal, hydroelectric, or atomic-energy stations. A proper supplied example

mathematics.independent_solution:
Classify by the primary energy source rather than a later shared rotating or
steam stage:

- Station Jia: fuel thermal. Its input is fuel chemical energy; the described
  release of heat, steam drive, and generator drive gives chemical -> thermal
  -> mechanical -> electrical energy.
- Station Yi: hydroelectric. Flowing water supplies mechanical energy to the
  water turbine, which mechanically drives the generator -> electrical energy.
  No chemical-energy combustion of water occurs in this description.
- Station Bing: atomic-energy. Nuclear energy supplies heat, then steam/turbine
  mechanical drive and electrical generation: nuclear -> thermal -> mechanical
  -> electrical energy. Steam downstream does not turn its primary input into
  fuel chemical energy or make it fuel thermal in the lesson's taxonomy.

This is a solution of supplied hypothetical mechanisms, not recall of named
large or historical stations. The particular nuclear case explicitly uses
steam; it does not assert that every nuclear station must do so.

Complete true set: `{A, C, E}`. All three, and only those three, must be selected.
